\chapter{Haan Sa: A Respectful Yes, Sign by Sign}
\label{ch:mw-haan-saa}
\hlchaptermodality{3}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can recognise, hear, say, copy, and independently write \mw{हां} \mw{सा} as a respectful affirmative answer.}

A source-attested polite affirmative built from two tiny script steps and the already-known respect word \mw{सा}, followed by independently scored four-skill retrieval.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[ha]{\mw{ह} — \emph{ha}, one new sign}

\label{lesson:MW-W03-ha}



\begin{quote}
Give the Chapter 1 greeting reply from memory. Then, with \textbf{\mw{आभार}} covered, say it as formal thanks and write it once. Uncover only long enough to check each sign.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one sign and one sound}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ह}} — \emph{ha}
\end{quote}

Let the air pass freely as you say \emph{ha}. Do not add the rest of the coming word yet; today the eye, ear, voice, and hand meet only \textbf{\mw{ह}}.

\subsection*{Writing — observe, trace, copy}
1. look at \textbf{\mw{ह}} for three seconds 2. finger-trace its lower curve and upright line 3. copy \textbf{\mw{ह}} twice 4. say \emph{ha} after each copy

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Cover the model for five seconds. Write \textbf{\mw{ह}}, uncover, and compare.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[nasal mark]{\mw{ं} — a small dot for the nasal ending}

\label{lesson:MW-W03-anusvara}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{ह}}, then \textbf{\mw{भ}}, from memory. Add the familiar long-\emph{ā} mark to \textbf{\mw{ह}}: \textbf{\mw{हा}}. Read it once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one small new mark}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ं}} — a dot above
\end{quote}

In the source spelling \textbf{\mw{हां}}, this dot cues the nasal ending. Say \emph{hā(n)} slowly: the vowel is long and the ending resonates through the nose. Speakers vary, so listen for the whole word rather than forcing one exaggerated sound.

\subsection*{Writing — add only the mark}
1. copy \textbf{\mw{हा}} once 2. look at \textbf{\mw{हां}} 3. add \textbf{\mw{ं}} above the end of your copy 4. compare the dot's position, then say \emph{hā(n)}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Hide \textbf{\mw{हां}} for five seconds. Write it once, then uncover and compare.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hā(n) sā]{\mw{हां} \mw{सा} — a respectful yes}

\label{lesson:MW-C03-haan-saa}



\begin{quote}
Say the Chapter 1 greeting from memory. Write \textbf{\mw{हां}}, then \textbf{\mw{सा}}, as two separate known pieces.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{The exchange — join the two pieces}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा।}} — \emph{Hā(n) sā.} — Yes, respectfully.
\end{quote}

The first word answers yes. Familiar \textbf{\mw{सा}} keeps the answer respectful. A scholarly Marwari text edition identifies \emph{hā(n)-sā} as the polite affirmative, and a Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi dialogue writes \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} in context.

\subsection*{Writing — guided, then delayed}
1. copy \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} once while looking 2. point to the space between the answer and the respect word 3. hide the phrase for ten seconds 4. write \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} from memory 5. compare \textbf{\mw{हां}}, the space, and \textbf{\mw{सा}} separately

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Say \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} once without looking, then write it once with the model covered.

Sources: \href{https://hasp.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/catalog/view/1151/2059/103085}{Hess, \emph{Texts and Translations}} and \href{https://rbssa.artandculture.rajasthan.gov.in/content/dam/doitassets/art-and-culture/Rajasthani-Bhasha-Sahitya-Avm-Sanskriti-Academy-Bikaner/pdf/JJ\_All\_Pdf/JJ\_47\_01\_02\_April\_to\_May\_2019.pdf}{Rajasthan Sahitya Akademi, \emph{Jāgtī Jot}, April–May 2019}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hā(n) sā]{Listen and answer — yes without the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C03-listen-say}



\begin{quote}
Write the first sign of \textbf{\mw{आभार}}, then the first sign of \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}}. Say which belongs to formal thanks and which begins a yes answer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: answer by ear}
Have someone or a screen reader say these in either order: \emph{ābhār} and \emph{hā(n) sā}. Without looking, point left for formal thanks and right for respectful yes. Then say \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} as the answer to a question you accept.

\subsection*{Your turn — four tiny skills}
1. \textbf{Listen:} identify \emph{hā(n) sā} without seeing it. 2. \textbf{Speak:} answer yes respectfully without reading. 3. \textbf{Read:} choose \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} from \textbf{\mw{आभार} · \mw{हां} \mw{सा} · \mw{राम}}. 4. \textbf{Write:} cover all models and write only \textbf{\mw{हां}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Close the page. Say \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}}, then write \textbf{\mw{हां}} from memory.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Practice — hear a yes, give a yes}

\label{lesson:MW-C03-practice}



\begin{quote}
With the page covered, write \textbf{\mw{भ}}, then \textbf{\mw{हां}}. Say \textbf{\mw{आभार}} for formal thanks; say \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}} for a respectful yes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn — independent four-skill check}
1. \textbf{Listen:} hear \emph{hā(n) sā} and identify an affirmative answer, without text. 2. \textbf{Speak:} hear “Will you come?” and answer yes respectfully, without notes. 3. \textbf{Read:} cover the English and explain \textbf{\mw{हां} \mw{सा}}. 4. \textbf{Write:} hear \emph{hā(n) sā}, wait fifteen seconds, then write the complete phrase.

Score each line separately. A missed line is the one to repeat; three stronger skills do not erase a writing or listening miss.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built — and what remains}]
You can now give one respectful affirmative. You have not yet learnt the Marwadi responses for no or okay, and you have not completed a yes/no exchange. Those remain separate tiny steps.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
If the dot or \textbf{\mw{ह}} stalled, return only to its two-minute sign lesson before trying the complete dictation again.
\end{tcolorbox}
